cases.scenario: Install a test extension that depends on a second extension. Start the same profile with a supported option override, then try a missing dependency, a duplicate ID and an incompatible version.
expected: Valid declarations resolve deterministically and the option changes only the advertised capability. The public manifest exposes the resolved dependencies and effective configuration.
Invalid configurations fail before dispatch or document publication, with a diagnostic identifying the rejected declaration.

cases.scenario: Configure a custom mark and a bounded custom block with typed fields, a renderer and an HTML converter through the documented SDK. Insert and edit each from a host command, then reopen and interchange the document.
expected: The nodes and marks retain their approved fields, identifiers and formatting through live rendering, export and compatible restore. A supported field edit is one undoable command.
A consumer without the required extension receives the documented compatibility outcome and an actionable diagnostic. It never silently treats an unsupported custom node as another type.
cases.untrustedInput: Pass an invalid field and an unapproved external reference through the extension converter. Verify validation is applied before editor, history or publishable state changes.

cases.scenario: Register a typed extension command with a distinct keyboard binding and invoke it by its shortcut and host control. In a fresh editor attempt to compile two identical chords, then restart with the extension disabled.
expected: The shortcut and host control dispatch the same admitted command and expose the same eligibility. The duplicate binding configuration is refused before listeners or editor DOM are installed.
Disabling the extension removes its keyboard registration. A failed or refused invocation leaves existing content and history unchanged.

cases.scenario: Install a presentation extension that renders a per-node placeholder or highlight from the current document state. Trigger rerendering and owner disposal, and repeat with a callback that throws.
expected: The decoration updates with semantic state and leaves stored content, selected text and exported data unchanged. Disposal releases listeners and presentation state without touching another editor.
A failing callback follows the documented isolation and fallback behavior. Commands and valid renderers continue working without a partial document write.

cases.scenario: Select a mixed inline formatting range, then apply the same command using a toolbar button and its advertised shortcut in separate runs. Repeat in a read-only editor.
expected: The toggle accurately announces mixed, active and disabled states, and keyboard and pointer invocation produce the same semantic result and history group.
The read-only control refuses the edit through both paths while leaving text selection and navigation available.

cases.scenario: Configure a toolbar with action groups, a labeled dropdown and a custom control. Resize from a wide layout to overflow, navigate with the keyboard and use an overflowed command.
expected: Configured grouping, order and accessible names remain discoverable. Overflowed commands retain the same active and disabled state and can be reached without pointer input.
Closing the dropdown or completing its action returns focus to the documented control or editor location. An unknown requested control is handled during configuration with the documented diagnostic.

cases.scenario: Select text by pointer and keyboard in a scrolling host, then resize the viewport near an edge and invoke a selection toolbar command. Collapse the selection and repeat in read-only mode.
expected: Eligibility and placement follow the documented selection and viewport behavior. Shown controls remain reachable at supported zoom and viewport sizes and act on the visible selection.
The overlay hides or updates when navigation invalidates the selection. Commit returns focus to the editor and creates one undoable action.

cases.scenario: Open the context menu using the advertised keyboard command and by pointer on text, image and table selections. Inspect the applicable controls and attempt one action after a shared update changes the selection.
expected: Each menu exposes controls appropriate to the current selection and provides named keyboard targets. Escape dismisses it with the original context focused.
A stale draft refuses the action instead of targeting a changed selection. A fresh context action and its fixed-toolbar equivalent have the same mutation and eligibility.

cases.scenario: Search for a fixture with accented letters, repeated whole words, partial matches and occurrences in a caption, a table cell and a collapsed section. Toggle case and whole-word flags, then navigate next, previous and wrap.
expected: Counts and highlights match the published Unicode, text-boundary and content-inclusion rules. The active result has a distinct indicator and can be located in the document from the search UI.
Read-only search retains navigation without offering an effective replace operation. Closing search restores focus to the documented location.

cases.scenario: Search code-like text that contains literal regex punctuation in both literal and regex modes. Run Replace One for an admitted capture pattern, then try an invalid regex.
expected: Literal mode searches the punctuation as text. The compiled pattern and replacement follow the documented regex and capture syntax, changing only the active eligible match.
An invalid query reports its error and clears or deactivates previous results as specified. It leaves document content and history unchanged.

cases.scenario: Search text in ordinary prose, table cells and protected content. Attempt Replace All after a peer changes a match, then repeat with fresh results spanning both editable and protected matches. Use a separate query of all eligible matches for the limit and success cases.
expected: A stale action, an oversized action and a mixed protected/editable action each refuse the entire change. The eligible action updates every match in its declared scope once and preserves unrelated content.
The successful action is one undoable history group. Undo after a compatible reopen restores the matching text while retaining unrelated peer edits.

cases.scenario: Configure an admitted mention trigger and its provider, return two candidates with identical labels and distinct identity keys, choose the second, then edit adjacent text and export.
expected: The inserted entity retains the chosen ID and remains an atomic editable item. Labels and the configured presentation survive recovery and supported interchange according to the output contract.
The same labels do not collapse two identities. Undo removes the mention as one edit and restores the trigger context where the published semantics specify it.
cases.untrustedInput: Return a label containing markup and an invalid or unauthorized identifier. Verify escaped labels and rejection of inadmissible entity data in edit, restore and export.

cases.scenario: Type two mention queries in quick succession while the first is pending. Resolve responses out of order and test Arrow keys, Enter, Escape and a provider failure using only the keyboard.
expected: Late or cancelled responses never replace the current query results. The active option and result state are announced through the supported accessibility contract.
Escape and provider failure preserve the typed text and leave focus usable. Selection commits only the currently resolved admitted candidate.

cases.scenario: Open an empty-block slash menu, filter for a block conversion, and apply it by keyboard. Repeat with no eligible match, a protected selection and a concurrent shared update.
expected: The successful action consumes its trigger and performs the conversion as one history step. Undo recovers the prior content and trigger as specified.
An empty, disabled or stale invocation leaves the document unchanged and returns an observable outcome without sending a partial command.

cases.scenario: Move a formatted block or container using its drag handle, then use the documented keyboard move path for the same destination. Include an adjacent block and a collaborator editing the moved block.
expected: Both valid paths retain the original block and metadata identities and produce the same semantic order. The live insertion target is visually distinguishable before commit.
Each commit creates one Undo step and preserves compatible collaborator edits. The moved content and positions agree after convergence and reopen.

cases.scenario: Begin dragging a block, hover inside its own descendant and outside the allowed scope, then cancel. Repeat with a concurrent target removal and an Escape cancellation during the keyboard move path.
expected: Invalid targets never advertise a valid insertion point. Refused or cancelled drops remove feedback and keep the previous content, identities and history.
Focus returns to the documented source handle or valid editor position, and a subsequent valid move can proceed.

cases.scenario: Drag a formatted text range between paragraphs using native drag input. Compare the ordinary move with any advertised copy modifier and with dropping onto a protected destination.
expected: The drop indicator identifies the actual target without mutating the document before commit. A valid move preserves admitted formatting and deletes the original range exactly once. A valid copy keeps the source range.
A protected destination refuses the drop without losing the original data. Undo recovers source and destination text and formats for the successful move.

cases.scenario: Mount the advertised fixed, inline, contextual and separately hosted toolbar layouts in small and wide containers. Change the active editor while one external toolbar host stays mounted.
expected: Each installed layout renders controls in its documented location and visibility conditions. Focus and command eligibility follow the active editor and never leak to the previously bound owner.
Unmount removes the controls and keyboard bindings owned by that layout. Saved document data remains compatible across the offered layouts of the same profile.

cases.scenario: Open the menu bar and operate nested or grouped items using the published arrow, typeahead, Escape and Tab controls. Repeat with right-to-left chrome and the supported screen reader pairing.
expected: Focus has a predictable roving tab stop, item roles and disabled state are announced, and directional navigation matches the declared language direction.
A successful activation dispatches the same admitted command as its toolbar control and returns focus as documented. Dismissal performs no edit.

cases.scenario: Move the caret from ordinary text into an empty line that supports block insertion, open the floating block menu through its advertised shortcut, then type text or leave the block.
expected: The menu appears only in published contexts and its appearance does not take editing focus. Keyboard opening exposes named eligible commands and accepting one produces the expected undoable block edit.
Typing or moving away updates the menu without leaving stale controls or a hidden keyboard stop. It does not compete with a selection toolbar on a noncollapsed range.

cases.scenario: Open the keyboard shortcut dialog on two supported platforms with one configured extension. Navigate using keyboard and the supported screen reader, dismiss it, disable that extension and reopen.
expected: The dialog exposes its title and contains focus while open. Chords match the active platform and configuration, and disabled extensions' chords disappear.
Escape and the close control restore the prior editor focus or documented fallback. Opening and dismissal do not create history entries.
